party._xpComment: XP to the next level = xpBase + xpPerLevel*L + xpPerLevelSq*L^2; a knockout pays xpKoBase + xpKoPerLevel*L (up to double against higher levels), times xpEliteMultiplier for elite wilds and xpBossMultiplier for land bosses. An even fight is most of a level early on and about half a level by level 30. The partner out with the lead takes half; Pokémon in their balls take benchShare. A catch gives the lead catchXpShare of a knockout.
party._fieldComment: Every trainer has at most fieldLimit Pokémon out at once (the first ones in party order that can fight); the rest wait in their balls and come out as others faint or on a swap.

wild._eliteComment: eliteChance of wild spawns are elites: eliteLevels more levels (evolved if that passes an evolution), marked with a gold star.

battle._damageScaleComment: Every hit is scaled by damageScale so fights last a few exchanges instead of two or three moves.
battle._statusComment: poison ticks poisonDamageFraction of max HP every 2 s until cured (Poison and Steel types are immune); freeze stops a Pokémon for freezeSeconds (a Fire hit thaws it; Ice and Fire types are immune); confusion lasts confusionSeconds and sends each move off in a random direction confusionMissChance of the time.

styler._comment: Capture Styler: hold C and draw loops round a wild Pokémon. It needs baseLoops + 1 per perLevel levels (+eliteLoops for elites, +bossLoops for land bosses, at most maxLoops). A full set calms it for calmSeconds: it stops fighting and every ball thrown at it counts catchMultiplier times. The line reaches maxRange tiles from the trainer; if the Pokémon runs through the line it breaks and one loop is lost.

dodge._comment: Space (when nothing is in reach to talk to or pick up) dashes your lead dashTiles in the direction you move (or face) over dashSeconds; hits that land in the first safeSeconds miss. Rivals in one-on-one battles dodge telegraphed moves aiChance of the time.

duel._comment: One-on-one trainer battles: two trainers within startRange (and in sight) recall their parties and send out one Pokémon each. Trainers step apart to standGap; leads come out sendOut tiles in front; the fight stays within arenaRadius of the middle. The player steers the lead at monSpeed. A rival picks its next Pokémon after aiPickSeconds; zoom is the camera zoom while the player battles.

darkness._comment: Every pulseSeconds the safe circle shrinks to the next radius; the darkness creeps in at sweepTilesPerSecond (a trainer walks about 4.8).

sizes._comment: Pokémon are drawn to their Pokédex height against the trainers: a trainer sprite's body (trainerPx art pixels) stands trainerHeightM tall. Pokémon under smallFloorM are drawn on a ramp from smallBaseM (at 0 m) up to smallFloorM, so small ones stay readable and still smaller than bigger ones.
